persons.name: Harinātha
persons.evidence: manohara sūnunā gosvāminā harinātha kṛtāyāṃ vaidyajīvanaṭīkāyāṃ

date.as_written: miti āsvī dvitīyāṃ 2 maṃgalavāsare || || saṃvat || || 1890 || || vṛṣe śākha || || 17 || 14

notes: The copy date is internally inconsistent: VS 1890 corresponds to Śaka 1755, while Śaka 1714 corresponds to VS 1849; the cataloguer marks the '8' of 1890 as doubtful (18〈〈8〉〉90), so one figure is corrupt and the CE year cannot be fixed. The chronogram 'khaṃ vahni sindhubhir' (0-3-7, apparently one digit lost, i.e. VS 17[?]30-type date) with jyeṣṭha kṛṣṇa 7 bhṛguvāra is the composition date of Harinātha's ṭīkā, not the copy date. 'śrīnātha gosvāmibhīr' in the corrupt verse 'ṭīkā vaidyajīvanasya racī[tā] śrīnātha gosvāmibhiḥ' most likely refers again to the commentator Harinātha Gosvāmin (possibly 'śrī[hari]nātha'); not listed as a separate person. 'chaganajīvrane pustakalītaṃ pustakaṃ' is read as vernacular (Rajasthani/Gujarati 'līto' = taken): 'the book was taken/acquired by Chaganajī brāhmaṇa', hence tentatively an owner; the segmentation ('paṃḍītasya' may belong either to Puruṣottama or to Chaganajī) and the name are uncertain, -jī treated as honorific. 'śrī mutharaśa' is probably 'Mathureśa' (Kṛṣṇa), an invocation, not a person. Catalogue scribe field (Puruṣottama) agrees with the colophon. Language of the colophon mixes Sanskrit with vernacular (Hindi/Rajasthani) forms; no place or king named.
